scope: Preserve an unadmitted native listening turn across the existing LOCAL_STOP/capture-resume handshake.

change.mechanism: The native subclass preserves input generation and queued microphone prefix only while a user turn or settled fragment is unadmitted and no core work, greeting or output is pending. A one-use exemption applies to the immediately following native interrupt call. Busy output/work retains ordinary invalidation.

ownerRepeat.evidenceKind: Private capture and native service diagnostics; no raw conversation is published.
ownerRepeat.observedProblem: A final core answer existed but no literal speech request followed. The capture iterator ended early while the session continued.
ownerRepeat.causalityLimit: No wire LOCAL_STOP packet was explicitly recorded in that owner session. Early capture termination supports a native resume explanation; the corresponding generation invalidation is reproduced separately. The reason for the later approximately 30-second close remains unestablished.

deterministicReproduction.resultSource: Recorded tool stdout reported by the implementing worker; no raw pytest or replay stdout file was saved.
deterministicReproduction.explanation: The baseline native clear/interrupt invalidates generation 1 before its final transcript arrives. The core still answers that input, but the response floor suppresses its speech.

checks: Preserve open input and queued prefix when only listening.
Preserve a finalized fragment during its existing quiet-settlement interval.
Pending core work, queued speech, active output and greeting retain interruption invalidation.
The actual inherited LOCAL_STOP handler restarts capture and yields one complete answer.
The preservation exemption is consumed once.
Inherited END_SESSION and MUTED close during pending or completed answers without late speech.
Existing wake/readiness and authority recovery checks remain green.
offlineValidation.evidenceLimit: Pass counts and durations were retained from tool output in the private assessment, not a raw pytest log. Two initial recovery-fixture import failures were corrected to use actual /opt/eva precedence before the passing run.

controlledLive.route: One prerecorded synthetic input through the existing realtime recognizer, NativeCodexMediaSession, provisioned household core binding and existing literal HA TTS; paced software PCM output.
controlledLive.intervention: Invoke the native clear_user_turn/interrupt capture-resume pair about 400 ms after the first provider user turn starts; restart capture at its retained input offset. This is software injection, not an observed physical wire control.

timing.clock: All values below use the same harness monotonic clock.
timing.signalDefinition: First submitted PCM frame with absolute signed-16-bit peak greater than 80; not exact acoustic onset.

developmentUsage.note: Development test traffic. One core request is not a claim of one underlying model request. Costs and unreported usage remain unknown.

installation.coreContainerUnchangedScope: At this speaker installation only. Another executor replaced the core afterward; this receipt does not claim the later core container remained unchanged.

limits: The software reproduction and controlled live test establish this listening-resume repair, not that every physical input failure has the same cause.
No physical speaker output, room microphone quality, free spoken barge-in or owner acceptance is established.
The native echo guard remains active; this change does not implement ordinary speech interruption during Eva output.
The measured 8.845-second input-end to first signal delay is not a whole-voice latency acceptance.
Independent acoustic word fidelity was not remeasured in this run.
Private raw capture, request identifiers and transcripts remain outside the repository.
